questions.q: Which of these nouns is feminine?
choices: מַחְבֶּרֶת
סֵפֶר
כֶּלֶב
שׁוּלְחָן
questions.why: A noun ending in an unstressed ה or in ת is feminine, and almost everything else is masculine. There is no article to tell you the way French has le and la, so the ending is the whole of your evidence.

questions.q: What gender is יָד, and why?
choices: feminine, because it is a body part that comes in a pair
masculine, because it has no feminine ending
masculine, because it is one syllable
feminine, because every short noun is
questions.why: יָד, רֶגֶל, עַיִן, אוֹזֶן and שֵׁן are feminine with no ending at all. The pairing is a memory hook, not a rule: עִיר, אֶרֶץ and דֶּרֶךְ are feminine too and nobody has two of them.

questions.q: Which noun ends in ה and is masculine anyway?
choices: לַיְלָה
תְּמוּנָה
שָׁנָה
מִשְׁפָּחָה
questions.why: לַיְלָה breaks the ending rule, and so does כִּיסֵּא despite its alef. The exceptions are few enough to learn one at a time, which is why every vocabulary entry in this course carries its gender.
Masculine nouns take ־ִים, but a segolate does not simply gain an ending: the whole inside of the word reshuffles. מֶלֶךְ behaves the same way and becomes מְלָכִים.
The feminine plural is ־וֹת, and it replaces the singular ה rather than sitting on top of it. תְּמוּנָה becomes תְּמוּנוֹת the same way.
A masculine noun with a feminine-looking plural. The ending changed and the gender did not, which is why big tables are שׁוּלְחָנוֹת גְּדוֹלִים. מָקוֹם and חַלּוֹן do exactly the same.
The word is replaced outright, and the result looks masculine while staying feminine. It is one of the most frequent nouns in the language, so this is the irregular plural to burn in first.
Simply irregular, like אִישׁ becoming אֲנָשִׁים and בֵּן becoming בָּנִים. The ending is the ordinary masculine one; it is the stem underneath that has been rebuilt.

choices: נָשִׁים יָפוֹת, because נָשִׁים is feminine
נָשִׁים יָפִים, because נָשִׁים ends in ־ִים
נָשִׁים יָפָה, because it is one group
either one; both are heard
questions.why: Agreement follows the noun's real gender, never the shape of its ending. נָשִׁים יָפִים is wrong and unmistakably foreign, and it is the single pair worth memorising out of this chapter.

questions.q: Why is "two eyes" עֵינַיִים and not עֵינִים?
choices: eyes come in a pair, so they take the dual ending
עַיִן is feminine, so its plural is irregular
עֵינִים would be the plural of a different word
the dual is used for anything you cannot count
questions.why: Hebrew has a third number for things that naturally come in twos: יָדַיִים, רַגְלַיִים, נַעֲלַיִים, מִשְׁקָפַיִים. For body parts it is the ordinary plural, so you do not say יָדִים at all.

questions.q: Three days is שְׁלוֹשָׁה יָמִים, not a dual. What does that tell you about the dual on a time word?
choices: it means exactly two and nothing else
it is used for any small number
it replaces the plural of time words
it is only used in writing
questions.why: יוֹמַיִים is two days and שְׁבוּעַיִים is two weeks, precisely. The dual is a closed set of words you learn one by one; you are never asked to invent a new one.
The describing word comes after the noun in Hebrew, and it agrees with what the noun is rather than what it looks like. Feminine plural noun, feminine plural ending on the word beside it.
Both are duals, and both keep the double yod in full spelling. The וְ on the front of the second word is glued to it, one word on the page and one word in the ear.
Glasses are a dual because they come as a pair, like מִכְנָסַיִים for trousers. The stress lands on the ending: mish-ka-FA-yim.

questions.q: Name three nouns whose plural ending belongs to the other gender, and say what gender each one really is.
a: שׁוּלְחָן takes שׁוּלְחָנוֹת and stays masculine, as do מָקוֹם with מְקוֹמוֹת and חַלּוֹן with חַלּוֹנוֹת. Going the other way, אִישָּׁה takes נָשִׁים, שָׁנָה takes שָׁנִים and מִילָּה takes מִילִּים, and all three stay feminine.
questions.why: The ending is a good guess for gender in the singular and a bad one in the plural. Since the gender decides every adjective, verb and number attached to the noun, it is worth looking a word up rather than reading it off the ending.
